newsitem.title: FRANCE: Corsica tax haven plan approved hours after bomb.
newsitem.headline: Corsica tax haven plan approved hours after bomb.

text.p: The French government approved on Wednesday a plan to transform Corsica into a tax haven to spur economic development on the Mediterranean resort island, which is racked by separatist guerrilla violence.
Just hours before the cabinet met, an explosion badly damaged a nightclub in northern Corsica amid a series of guerrilla attacks in a 20-year campaign to obtain greater autonomy from mainland France.

Cabinet approval clears the way for parliamentary action on the government's tax haven proposal, which officials said would benefit 95 percent of Corsica's businesses and cost the state some three billion francs ($600 million) over five years.
Local business leaders and trade unions have argued that the tax incentives would be useless without an end to separatist violence.

The bomb on Wednesday exploded inside the Stella club, which had been closed for renovation, on the Arinella beach near Bastia shortly after midnight. There were no injuries and no one immediately claimed responsibility for the attack.
On Monday night, suspected Corsican separatists fired shots at a gendarmerie barracks and set off four bombs on the island.
The "Historic Wing" of the Corsican National Liberation Front (FLNC) claimed responsibility for machine-gunning the gendarmerie barracks.

Urban Affairs Minister Jean-Claude Gaudin said the goal of the tax haven proposal was to "give a signal of hope to all those in Corsica who want to work for the island's future and who agree to a dialogue with the public authorities".
Gaudin insisted the government was committed to helping the island but could not go too far for fear of giving Corsica too great an advantage over other regions.

President Jacques Chirac told ministers he hoped the measure would help boost the island's economy and compared the plan to the creation of enterprise zones which already exist in mainland France, government spokesman Alain Lamassoure told reporters.

The tax-haven plan, approved by the European Commission, would exempt companies located in Corsica from corporate and income tax, up to certain limits, on industrial, commercial and agricultural activity.

Businesses would also be exempted from local business tax up to a fixed ceiling and would receive a partial refund of employer social security contributions in exchange for training young people and ending illegal labour.
